A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RecInter study and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-D. Matching material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation comparisons, ablations, and behavioral analyses in Section 4 and Appendix B, plus a human evaluation in Appendix B.7 and Table 8.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulation and human-evaluation results, including the benchmark comparisons and 30-pair human evaluation.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same multidimensional profiling, perceptual and cognitive memory, action selection, dynamic item updates, merchant agents, and CoT fine-tuning pipeline. No method component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both retain GoogleLocal's California restaurant subset, MovieLens, and AmazonBook. The interaction, malicious-review, merchant-response, brand-loyalty, and popularity-boost scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: RecAgent, Agent4Rec, and SimUSER remain the comparators in Tables 1 and 5. The base-model and recommendation-algorithm comparison sets in Tables 3 and 4 also match.

E3.justification: Both retain the same 1,000-agent evaluation, 20 candidate items, interaction ratios, metrics, and default 10-step simulation. Training, preprocessing, LLM judging, and human-evaluation settings in Appendices A and B are unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations, interaction tests, brand and popularity interventions, merchant-response study, sentiment analysis, model and recommender analyses, and Appendix C cases are all retained without revision.

E5.justification: Point estimates and human-LLM agreement reporting are unchanged. No repeated-run or seed counts, uncertainty intervals, or statistical tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1-5 and 8 retain their result entries. For example, RecInter's GoogleLocal 1:1 accuracy remains 0.7143, its adjusted LLM win rate remains 0.6917, and human-LLM agreement remains 26/30. Plotted trends and qualitative case findings also match.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, profile definitions, memory-scoring equation in Section 3, and adjusted-win-rate formula in Appendix B.6 are unchanged. No assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about dynamic user/merchant interaction, improved simulation credibility, and reproduction of Brand Loyalty and the Matthew Effect.

C2.justification: The interpretations of interaction effects and conservative review behavior are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning profiling bias, fixed action spaces, omitted social/external interactions, and bias propagation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a linked RecInter GitHub repository at the end of the abstract, providing a code-access pointer absent from v1. Appendix A's implementation and training details and Appendix D's prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain identical. Bibliography entries shift after the added acknowledgments, but no references or relationships to prior work are added or removed.

P1.justification: v2 corrects 'our integrates' to 'we integrate,' adjusts author/affiliation and email formatting, and adds an Acknowledgments paragraph before References. The remaining prose and substantive section structure are retained.

P2.justification: The author block is reformatted, the abstract gains a repository-link icon, and the acknowledgments cause bibliography reflow. Figures, tables, captions, and their placement remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new repository pointer improves implementation discoverability, and the acknowledgments disclose funding and computing support. Together with the small grammar and formatting corrections, these provide a limited documentation and transparency improvement. Scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged; repository contents and usability are not established by the PDFs.
